designSummary: Segmented regression of quarterly proportions, 17 quarters before and 14 after the change.
sampleSize: About 400 later episodes give about 12 per quarter, 200 before and 200 after. With recognition near 45 percent before and 70 percent after, a two-period comparison would have more than 95 percent power, but the segmented model is less precise: with 17 and 14 quarterly points and moderate autocorrelation, a level change of 20 percentage points is detectable with about 80 percent power. A change of 10 points would not be distinguishable from noise.
primaryAnalysis: Segmented binomial regression of quarterly recognition with terms for pre-existing trend, level change and slope change at March 2023, with autocorrelation checked and a pre-specified model.
secondaryAnalysis: The same model for unanticipated difficulty; alert presence described; recognition by emergency status, age band and language where recorded.
missingData: Episodes with missing anaesthetic records are counted and reported; not imputed.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; secondary outcomes reported with intervals.
software: R; analysis code fixed before extraction.
overfittingGuards: One change point fixed in advance
No search for alternative change points
summary: About 400 episodes; a 20-point level change is detectable, a 10-point change is not.
